headword: {御朱印帳|ごしゅいんちょう}

definitions.gloss: temple and shrine stamp book; goshuin book
definitions.explanation: A special accordion-fold booklet used to collect goshuin — calligraphic stamps and inscriptions given at Buddhist temples and Shinto shrines as proof of visit and prayer.

examples.english: I carry my goshuin book with me every trip and collect stamps from temples and shrines around the country.

notes:
A {御朱印帳|ごしゅいんちょう} is typically a beautifully bound accordion-fold (じゃばら) book made of thick Japanese paper. Each page receives a ⟦{御朱印|ごしゅいん}→御朱印：16927_goshuin⟧ — a combination of a red seal stamp and hand-brushed calligraphy with the temple or shrine name and the date of visit. Collecting ⟦{御朱印|ごしゅいん}→御朱印：16927_goshuin⟧ has become a popular hobby and a way to enjoy temple and shrine tourism.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditionally, ⟦{御朱印|ごしゅいん}→御朱印：16927_goshuin⟧ were given as proof that a pilgrim had copied and offered a sutra. Today they are available to any visitor for a small fee (typically 300-500 yen). Many shrines and temples sell their own unique {御朱印帳|ごしゅいんちょう} with distinctive cover designs.
